title: Walkthrough request — Chapter 1: Salt and Sorrow

posts.cooked:
Hey everyone! I just started playing through Chapter 1: Salt and Sorrow, and I’m finding myself a bit stuck on the part where you have to navigate the flooded ruins to find the lost relic. I’ve tried a few different paths, but every time I think I’m close, I get swarmed by those shadowy guardians and have to backtrack. If anyone has a clear walkthrough or some tips on the safest route, that would be awesome.

Also, on a side note—has anyone else noticed that the voice-acting in this chapter is seriously impressive? The way the narrator shifts tone depending on the time of day really pulls me into the atmosphere. Would love to hear your favorite moments or lines from this bit if you’re into the voice-over side of things too! Hoping to get through this chapter soon so I can dive deeper into the story. Thanks in advance for any help!

posts.cooked:
Hey! I just finished Chapter 1: Salt and Sorrow yesterday, and I’m happy to help with your walkthrough. The part where you have to navigate the cliffs with the slippery rocks can be super tricky if you don’t pause often to let your stamina recover. Make sure to time your jumps carefully, and don’t rush — the game really punishes missed leaps here. Also, keep an eye out for those hidden alcoves along the path; they sometimes have little voice logs that give extra background on the lore and can clue you in on what to expect next.

As for voice-acting, I noticed they really leaned into the emotional weight at the campfire scene. If you’re recording or just trying to replicate it for fan-works, try to match the pacing of the dialogue there — it’s slower and more deliberate, which helps convey the sorrow and tension that set the mood for the rest of the chapter. It’s such a great detail that makes the story feel more immersive rather than just a simple quest.

If you get stuck on the riddle with the salt crystals, here’s a tip: the order you activate them matches the phases of the moon shown in the sky earlier in the chapter. It’s subtle, but once you notice it, solving that puzzle feels really rewarding. Hope this helps, and good luck with the next chapters!
